programme: TCF7L2, the canonical Wnt/β-catenin effector, sits atop a crypt/epithelial-progenitor axis (its target set includes CDX1, CDX2, MYC, CCND1, CTNNB1) that feeds into SOX9, itself a Wnt-responsive progenitor factor whose own target list includes SNAI2. SNAI2, together with TFAP2A, then runs an EMT-type epithelial-plasticity switch — both target the cadherin/junction machinery (CDH1, CDH2, CDH3, CDH5, JUP for SNAI2; CDH1, TP53BP1, ESR1, MMP2 for TFAP2A). MUC1 sits as the epithelial-membrane/mucin readout of the same module: its short target list (CDKN1A, JUN, CCN2) matches the known MUC1-C intracellular signalling arm rather than a broad TF programme. Together: TCF7L2→SOX9 progenitor drive, SOX9/SNAI2/TFAP2A EMT-plasticity switch, MUC1 as epithelial-surface/signalling output.
role_in_a: In IBS, this axis would sit in the colonic crypt: TCF7L2-driven progenitor renewal and MUC1-associated mucus/glycocalyx maintenance repairing a mucosa under low-grade injury, with SNAI2/TFAP2A-mediated epithelial plasticity modulating barrier permeability. The record's support for this in IBS is genetic-association only (TCF7L2 and MUC1 GWAS hits), not a mechanistic study of the module acting together.
role_in_b: In thymoma, the same progenitor/EMT toolkit would map onto thymic epithelial cell proliferation and the EMT-like dedifferentiation associated with more invasive thymic epithelial tumour subtypes. MUC1 (epithelial membrane antigen) and SOX9 carry the strongest computational placement here (Open Targets percentile 0.83 and 0.95 of thymoma-scored genes), consistent with an epithelial-tumour programme, but no retrieved paper documents this mechanism for thymoma specifically.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve a simple/glandular epithelium — colorectal mucosa versus thymic epithelium — where a Wnt-progenitor/EMT-plasticity module governs the balance between renewal and dedifferentiation. If this module is active in patient subgroups of both diseases, it more likely reflects convergent reuse of a generic epithelial-plasticity toolkit in two unrelated epithelia than any disease-specific link between IBS and thymoma.
reasoning: The five carrying factors form a nameable, internally consistent programme (Wnt/TCF7L2→SOX9 progenitor axis feeding an SNAI2/TFAP2A EMT switch with MUC1 as epithelial output), and some are independently placed in one or both diseases by Open Targets. But nothing retrieved connects the module to thymoma mechanistically — every thymoma-relevant number is a computed association score, not literature — and the two on-point PMIDs for IBS are genetic-association GWAS hits, not evidence of the module operating as a unit. IBS is also not classically an epithelial-proliferative/EMT disease, so the pairing with a thymic epithelial neoplasm is not obvious from anatomy or clinical practice, which is why this reads as unexpected rather than supported, and weak rather than moderate.
support: 33608531 — GWAS of peptic ulcer disease/other GI disorders places MUC1 among genes associated with IBS (genetic association, not mechanistic). 31691451 — associates TCF7L2 (GLP-1/CCK receptor pathway) variants with GI symptoms including IBS (genetic association). No PMID in the retrieved set ties any carrying factor to thymoma; the Open Targets percentiles for SOX9 (0.9483), SNAI2 (0.8851) and MUC1 (0.8339) in thymoma are computational disease-association scores, not literature evidence, and TFAP2A has no Open Targets association in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Stain thymoma resections for nuclear SOX9, SNAI2/TFAP2A and membrane MUC1(EMA), and check whether tumours with high TCF7L2-target-gene activity (CDX2, MYC, CCND1) co-express SNAI2/TFAP2A with cadherin-switching (loss of CDH1, gain of CDH2/CDH3); if IBS mucosal biopsies with elevated MUC1/TCF7L2-target expression do not also show this co-expression pattern, or the ReMap-bound target sets for TCF7L2/SOX9/SNAI2/TFAP2A show no enrichment among each other's targets in either tissue, the shared-module account is refuted.
caveats: Colorectal and thymic tissue are anatomically and functionally distant (a functional bowel disorder versus an epithelial neoplasm). 40 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 1 independent cohort pair, so counts like NFIA's 36/40 or MUC1's 33/40 reflect repeated internal subgroup splits, not independent replications. ZBTB17 was discordant (31/40) and excluded from the carrying set. The single-view and tissue-generic exclusion lists were not provided with this pair, so it cannot be confirmed what else was screened out before ranking. NFIA, ID2, ZNF165, GLIS3, ETS2 and discordant ZBTB17 do not fit the epithelial-plasticity programme and are not used to carry this account.
